messages.subject: Linear predictors
parts:
Hi Help,
 
I want to ask a simple question about the number of linear predictors in the output of inla.posterior.sample() function.
For example if the model is f  <- resp ~ 0 + Intercept + x1 + x2 + f(i,model=spde), the latent term in the output seems to include the following variables,
Preditor.0001, Predictor.0002,..., i.0001,i.0002,..., Intercept.1, x1.1, x2.1... 
I understand the number of i.xxxx is mesh$n, but I am confused with the number of Predictor.xxxx, which is a larger number than the effects in my stack function. Would you mind explaining a little bit more about the contents of the Predictor.xxxx? So that I know which to be included as the samples of the response.
 
Many thanks,
David

messages.author: afb003e064114795
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Linear predictors
parts:
The basic linear predictor is called eta, and the one constructed with the help of the stack is eta^* = A %*% eta.
I think the output is first eta^* and then eta, I.e. the Predictor.xxxx output is the combination of the two etas.

Finn
